allowedSourceMaterial.overview: A self-indulgent private investigator winds up on a cruise ship full of rich patrons, gorgeous women, murderous terrorists, and scarce food.

facts.overview: A self-indulgent private investigator winds up on a cruise ship full of rich patrons, gorgeous women, murderous terrorists, and scarce food.
facts.title: City Hunter

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Trapped on the high seas with ruthless gunmen and no rations, can a frivolous private eye outwit danger before the voyage goes completely off course?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: In Wong Jing's 1993 Hong Kong action comedy, a self-indulgent private investigator winds up trapped aboard a luxury cruise liner alongside wealthy socialites, glamorous passengers, scarce food, and ruthless terrorists.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Fast, comedic action with low emotional weight, perfectly built for a high-energy, easygoing group watch.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Wong Jing delivers a fast, breezy blend of martial-arts action and broad farce, turning a high-stakes cruise hostage crisis into an energetic, lighthearted thrill ride.

issueSummaries: curiosityHook and description both say the protagonist is 'trapped' (aboard a luxury cruise liner / 'on the high seas'). The overview says only that he 'winds up on a cruise ship'. Confinement is a mechanic the packet does not state. curiosityHook also says 'no rations' where the overview says 'scarce food', and 'ruthless gunmen' where it says 'murderous terrorists'. The gunmen framing introduces a weapon attribute the packet does not state.

whyWatch calls the situation a 'cruise hostage crisis'. 'Hostage' appears only in facts.keywords, and allowedSourceMaterial.keywords is empty. The overview mentions terrorists but no hostages, so this imports a specific plot mechanic from keyword-only material.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. 'Trapped' is idiomatic for being on a ship full of murderous terrorists, and 'hostage crisis' is a plausible reading of terrorists on a cruise ship, so an adjudicator could approve on that basis. I flag the fields because the same escalation (a specific confinement or hostage mechanic) recurs across three fields, and because 'hostage' has no authorized source. If Sophia treats facts.keywords as valid grounding, the 'hostage' concern would weaken, though 'trapped', 'gunmen' and 'no rations' would remain. 'Luxury cruise liner' and 'glamorous passengers' were considered and left within tolerance.
